findings.title: U1 pin EN is floating / undriven
findings.failure_mode: A floating EN/CHIP_PU leaves the module in an indeterminate reset state — unreliable or no boot.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet + hardware design guidelines: EN (CHIP_PU) must be pulled up (typ. 10k) with a delay cap; it must not float or the module may not boot reliably.

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 100n
findings.failure_mode: A 1uF (instead of 100nF) cap on IO0 defeats the auto-download/reset sequence — can't flash without manual BOOT.
findings.citation: ESP32 auto-program circuit: IO0 uses a 100nF cap. A 1uF cap here (as on EN) is too large and breaks the auto-download timing.

findings.title: DevKit powered on both 5V pin and 3V3 pin simultaneously (paralleled regulators)
findings.detail:
U1 pin 21 (5V) is fed from the board +5V rail (U3 LM7805), and U1 pins 1/2 (3V3) are tied through 0Ω R31 to the board +3.3V rail driven by U16 AP2112K-3.3. The DevKit's onboard LDO therefore drives its 3V3 output directly into the AP2112 output. The datasheet says the 5V and 3V3 supply inputs are mutually exclusive. Also, when USB is plugged in, the DevKit's USB 5V meets the board's +5V.

Second opinion (unsure): The netlist shows only R31.1 on the DevKit 3V3 net and gives no value for R31 or any connection from R31.2 to U16's output, so the 0Ω tie to the AP2112 rail is unverified; even if it exists, two 3.3V LDOs in parallel normally do not damage each other (LDOs source current but do not sink it), and 'mutually exclusive' on p.106 is a usage recommendation rather than proof of a board-killing fault.
findings.failure_mode: Two LDO outputs fight each other, which causes back-feeding, uneven current sharing and possible regulator stress. Plugging in USB can back-feed the 7805 output.

findings.title: U15 channel B (pins 5,6,7) left unconnected
findings.detail: Only amplifier 1 of the dual OPA2810 in U15 is used, as a unity-gain buffer driving CENTER_BIAS. The netlist shows no connection at all on VIN2+ (pin 5), VIN2- (pin 6) or VO2 (pin 7). If amplifier 2 is not needed, connect it as a buffer (tie pin 7 to pin 6) and tie pin 5 to ground or to a mid-supply voltage.
findings.failure_mode: A floating FET-input amplifier can drift to a rail or oscillate. That raises supply current and couples noise into amplifier 1 and the CENTER_BIAS reference.
findings.excerpt: VIN2+ 5 I Amplifier 2 noninverting input pin

findings.title: No datasheet available for DS1 (ILI9341 module)
findings.detail: No datasheet could be found for DS1, the ILI9341 14-pin SPI TFT/touch module, so its pins couldn't be checked against the manufacturer's spec. These connections still need a review against the module's datasheet: the LED backlight pin is driven directly from GPIO17, so check how much current it draws. The display and touch controller share SCK and MOSI (GPIO4 and GPIO5), the display's SDO pin is left unconnected, and VCC is on +3.3V.
findings.failure_mode: Without the datasheet, problems such as backlight current above what the GPIO can supply, or an unexpected supply or level requirement, can't be ruled out.

findings.title: TS5A23157 datasheet unavailable; SW3 not audited against it
findings.detail: No datasheet could be found for SW3 (TS5A23157), so its pinout, supply rating (+3.3V on V+), and signal ranges on COM1/COM2 (AD9833 outputs) could not be checked against the manufacturer's specifications.
findings.failure_mode: A pinout or rating error on SW3 would go unnoticed. That could break the routing of the function-generator signals.

findings.title: U1 pin EN has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing EN pull-up => no defined power-on reset delay.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: EN uses a ~10k pull-up to 3V3 plus a 1uF delay cap (RC reset).

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing IO0 pull-up can leave the module entering download mode unexpectedly.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: IO0 (boot strap) needs a pull-up (typ. 10k) so the module boots to flash by default.

findings.title: U1 pin 3V3 is on 'Net-(R31-Pad1)', expected a net containing '3.3'
findings.failure_mode: Module supply off the 3.3V rail is out of spec.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet, Pin definitions (3V3): module supply is 3.3V.

dropped.title: DevKitC 3V3 output tied to external AP2112 3.3V rail via R31 (0Ω): two regulators in parallel
dropped.detail: The DevKitC's 3V3 header pins (U1.1/U1.2) are the output of the board's own on-board 3.3V LDO, which runs from the 5V pin (U1.21 on +5V). Through R31 (0Ω) they connect directly to +3.3V, which U16 (AP2112K-3.3) also drives. So two LDO outputs are tied together with no isolation. The stored datasheet is a collection of Espressif board guides, and I could not find the DevKitC-1 power-supply section in it to quote.
dropped.failure_mode: The two regulators will fight because their output setpoints differ slightly. The one set higher supplies all the current, and the other may be back-driven. This can make the current sharing and power-up order unpredictable, and back-feed one regulator when only part of the board is powered (for example, the DevKit powered over USB while the 5V input is off). If you meant the ESP32 to run from U16, remove R31 or leave it unpopulated and use the DevKit's own LDO, or feed only one supply path.

dropped.title: U15 amplifier B (pins 5–7) not connected – unused channel left floating
dropped.detail: Only channel A of U15 (OPA2810, dual) is used, as a unity-gain buffer driving CENTER_BIAS. Pins 5 (VIN2+), 6 (VIN2-) and 7 (VO2) do not appear in the netlist, so channel B's inputs are floating. This often happens when only symbol unit A is placed. TI's usual advice for an unused channel is to wire it as a buffer: VO2 tied to VIN2-, and VIN2+ tied to ground or mid-supply.
dropped.failure_mode: The floating FET inputs of channel B can drift, so the output may rail or oscillate. This adds supply current and heat, and can couple noise into the CENTER_BIAS buffer and the ±12V rails.
dropped.excerpt: VIN2+ 5 I Amplifier 2 noninverting input pin

dropped.title: VREF/RFB driven by ±12 V op-amps right at the AD5452 ±12 V absolute maximum
dropped.detail: VREF (pin 7) is driven by U4 OUT and RFB (pin 8) by U5A OUT. Both OPA2810s run from +12V/-12V and have rail-to-rail outputs. If either amplifier saturates (from a gain error, a fault, or startup), its output can swing to nearly ±12 V, which is the absolute maximum for VREF and RFB with no margin left. Confirm that the gained_func amplitude is limited well below ±10 V in every operating state, or add clamping.
dropped.failure_mode: If an amplifier saturates or the ±12 V rails run slightly high, VREF/RFB can go past the ±12 V absolute maximum, which may damage the DAC.
dropped.excerpt: VREF, RFB to GND −12 V to +12 V

dropped.title: ILI9341 module datasheet unavailable; DS1 not checked against a datasheet
dropped.detail: The tools could not find a datasheet for DS1, the ILI9341 14-pin SPI TFT/touch module. The pin connections could not be checked against a datasheet. Netlist observations for the engineer to confirm: VCC is on +3.3V. The LED backlight pin is driven directly by GPIO17, so confirm that the module has its own backlight transistor or resistor and check how much current the pin draws. SDO/MISO is not connected, so the display cannot be read back. The touch controller shares SCK/MOSI with the display and uses separate CS (GPIO18), DOUT (GPIO6) and IRQ (GPIO8) lines.
dropped.failure_mode: Errors in the module's supply, backlight or interface would not be caught.

dropped.title: TS5A23157 datasheet unavailable; SW3 not verified
dropped.detail: No datasheet could be found for SW3 (TS5A23157), so I could not check its pinout, V+ rating, logic thresholds or decoupling requirements against the manufacturer's specifications. The footprint is a custom module (ohmen:TS5A23157_Module), so the pin mapping also needs a manual check.
dropped.failure_mode: If the pin mapping or supply requirements differ from the datasheet, the DDS-to-function-generator signal routing could fail.
